subject: Request: Custom SLA exhibit + order form language for MedStream deployment
messages:
From: Oliver Barnes <oliver@medstream.example.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@medstream.com
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Custom SLA exhibit + order form language

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at MedStream is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the reserved capacity options. Procurement asked me to reach out with a formal request: we need a custom SLA exhibit (to attach to our enterprise MSA/SOW) and order form language that calls out an availability/latency carveout for our near-real-time clinical workflows.

Key asks from our side:
- 99.95% monthly availability target for the production model endpoint (multi-region failover acceptable).
- P99 latency target of <= 350ms for 1–512 token responses under dedicated capacity.
- Clear definition of maintenance windows and notification SLA (48 hours notice preferred for planned maintenance that may impact availability).
- Fallback / degraded-mode behavior and credit calculation for cross-region failovers and rolling upgrades.
- Evidence we can supply to procurement: SOC2 excerpt references (if relevant), regional failover test logs, and historical latency percentiles for comparable customers.

Can you share a draft exhibit + the order form redline path and tell us what evidence you can produce in the 2-week procurement window? If there are any requested exceptions (e.g., lower SLA for beta features), please enumerate them.

Appreciate it — Oliver
Oliver Barnes
Director, Platform Ops — MedStream Health
oliver@medstream.example.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Custom SLA exhibit + order form language

Hi Oliver —

Thanks — this is clear and helpful. I've looped in Hannah (ops / evidence) and Jordan (sales/product order form) to draft a concise SLA exhibit and an orderform redline that maps to your asks. High-level notes up front:

- 99.95% monthly availability: we can provision a dedicated, multi-AZ pool and commit to 99.95% regionally. We need to clarify whether you require cross-region (active-active) failover or a passive failover that triggers on regional outage. The credit table differs depending on the failover model.
- P99 latency: 350ms is aggressive but doable under dedicated capacity for typical prompt lengths. We will include a latency SLO with a note about sequence length distributions and tokenization assumptions; the exhibit will include the typical workload profile used to qualify the SLO.
- Maintenance windows / notifications: Redwood's standard policy is 72 hours for scheduled maintenance that may affect availability; we can offer 48 hours for planned maintenance tied to extended commits or enterprise SOW. Unscheduled emergency maintenance will be called out separately.
- Fallback / degraded mode: we'll propose a defined degraded-mode (reduced throughput + best-effort latency) and an automatic fallback to a regional-compatible model variant. The orderform will define credit calculations for both partial degradation and full regional outage.

Hannah — can you pull the evidence matrix (SOC2 excerpt, regional test summaries, and a sanitized latency percentile CSV) and indicate what we can commit to within a 10 business day turn? Jordan — I'll need a clean redline of the order form showing the exhibit attachment reference and a DocuSign-ready path.

I'll assemble the first draft and send to MedStream by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(t) +1 628 555 0192

Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custom SLA exhibit + order form language — evidence matrix

Tessa / Jordan,

Attaching a pared-down evidence matrix for procurement. Notes below:

1) SOC2: we can provide the SOC2 Type II summary page (control coverage and auditor statement). Full SOC2 report requires an NDA; procurement typically accepts the summary + auditor contact. (attachment: evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx)

2) Regional failover tests: we have recent regional failover logs from a comparable enterprise customer (sanitized timestamps + metrics). These demonstrate successful warm failover with <30s DNS/IP re-route in our standard configuration. We will include a 30s–90s detection window in the exhibit and note that customer-side DNS configuration affects total failover time.

3) Latency percentiles: included sample p50/p90/p99 aggregates for 1–512 token requests under dedicated pools. These numbers are representative but not contractual outside the SLO window; the exhibit will reference the qualifying test harness and tokenization assumptions. (attachment: Proposed_SLA_Exhibit_v1.docx contains the SLO language and qualifying test harness description)

Timeline: I can produce the SOC2 summary and sanitized failover logs within 3 business days. The latency percentile CSV will be ready in 5 business days.

Laura — legal redlines to the exhibit? If you can flag any exposure points (maintenance carveouts, force majeure, experimental-flag exclusions) that would be good to have up front.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Reliability Engineering | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com

Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custom SLA exhibit + order form language — draft redlines

Team,

I've reviewed Proposed_SLA_Exhibit_v1 and added a few protective clarifications in the redline PDF:
- Maintenance: add a definition for "planned maintenance" and require that customer signs off on any maintenance that would change the SLO baseline for >4 hours.
- Failure attribution: require a joint incident review to determine whether credits apply (prevents unilateral claims based solely on customer-side network factors).
- Exclusions: clarify experimental features and third-party integrations are out-of-scope for the availability SLO.
- Credit calculation: use monthly prorated credits tied to the dedicated capacity seat(s) in scope; include a cap equal to one month's committed fees.

Jordan — when you prepare the orderform redline, please reference the exhibit as "Exhibit B: Availability & Latency SLO" and add a checkbox for the customer to select cross-region active failover (adds an additional configuration fee).

I'll attach the redline (orderform_redlines.pdf) and a brief comment summary to the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custom SLA exhibit + order form language

Tessa / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed notes. A couple quick clarifications from procurement before we proceed to DocuSign:

1) Confirm the fallback window: your note referenced 30s–90s detection plus DNS effects. Will the exhibit state a deterministic detection window (we'd prefer 60s as a baseline) or a range?
2) Credit cap: procurement accepts cap = 1 month's committed fees, but they want an explicit carveout that if there is repeated systemic noncompliance (more than 3 incidents in a rolling 12 months) we reopen the SLA/credits conversation. Can Redwood commit to that review clause?
3) Active failover option: please include the additional configuration fee number (or range) in the orderform redline so procurement can budget.

If you can confirm these items this afternoon, we'll initiate an internal legal review and aim for DocuSign next Tuesday.

Oliver
Director, Platform Ops — MedStream Health
